name: After Effects Eye-Locked Zoom With Text Parenting
use_when: A talking-head Reel hook or statement needs a smooth zoom-in or zoom-out without subject drift.
Text should feel attached to the speaker or frame during a zoom.
A rotoscoped duplicate is layered over the original video and both must share the same motion.
avoid_when: The source is too low-resolution for the intended zoom.
The zoom crops the speaker's face, hands, captions, or proof.
The text should remain screen-fixed instead of moving with the footage.

timeline_pattern.pattern: set_eye_guide -> keyframe_final_scale_position -> set_start_zoom -> align_eyes_to_guide -> easy_ease -> speed_graph -> parent_text_or_rotoscope -> preview
timeline_pattern.eye_rule: Use a horizontal guide across the eyes and adjust Y position so the eyes stay on the same line during the move.
timeline_pattern.parenting_rule: Parent text layers to the video only when they should scale with the footage.
timeline_pattern.rotoscope_rule: Apply the same zoom keyframes or preset to both the original and the rotoscoped duplicate.

motion.rule: Animate scale and position together, then refine the speed graph so the zoom starts or settles smoothly.

keyframe_values.intro_zoom_out_duration: Around 1.0-1.5 seconds can work for a high-quality hook zoom-out.
keyframe_values.large_start_scale: A dramatic hook zoom-out can start around 185-190% if resolution and crop remain safe.
keyframe_values.small_zoom: Use smaller zoom-in/out presets for body emphasis rather than repeating the hook-scale move.
keyframe_values.easing: Use Easy Ease, then shape the speed graph so the motion is not linear.

sound.rule: Use a whoosh only if the zoom is meant to be felt; keep hook words intelligible.

captions.rule: Check captions after parented zooms because attached text and subtitles can collide differently than screen-fixed text.

color.rule: Zooming into footage should not reveal noise, softness, or skin-tone artifacts that were hidden at full scale.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use crop/scale or zoompan driven by an eye/focus point and preview the first frames for subject drift.
implementation.remotion: Store an eyeLineY or focusBox and animate scale/translate with an easing curve; apply the same transform to cutout and base layers.
implementation.blender: Use camera or object scale keyframes with an empty aligned to the eyes when compositing talking-head footage.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use keyframes on the base video and duplicate/cutout layer, keeping the eyes in the same screen position during the move.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Effect Controls or Dynamic Link/After Effects, add a guide line for the eyes, keyframe Scale and Position, Easy Ease the keyframes, and reuse a saved preset only after crop-safe review.

common_mistakes: Scaling the shot without correcting Y position so the eyes jump during the zoom.
Applying zoom to the original layer but not the rotoscope/cutout duplicate.
Parenting text that should have remained screen-fixed.
Dropping a preset at the wrong playhead position so the motion starts late.
Making a body zoom as aggressive as the hook zoom.
qc: The speaker's eyes stay aligned during the zoom.
Original and rotoscope/cutout layers share the same motion.
Text parented to the video still reads at phone size.
Captions, face, hands, and proof remain crop-safe.
The zoom curve is eased and does not feel linear or jolty.
